Aisha and I are going to play soccer. (We agreed to.)
그럼요. 열 시에 운동장에서 만나기로 했어요.
Of course. We agreed to meet at the sports field at 10.
geureomyo yeol sie undongjangeseo mannagiro haesseoyo
sm: "-기로 했어요" means "decided / agreed to …".
"-기로 했어요" means "decided / agreed to …".
qz: 친구와 약속한 일은? 가려고 해요 / 가기로 했어요

i: A soft way to suggest something. It is like "How about …?" or "Why don't you …?" in English.
A soft way to suggest doing something. It is like "How about …?" or "Why don't you …?" in English.
m: 동사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-는 게 어때요?"를 붙입니다. 받침과 관계없습니다. ㄹ 받침은 떨어집니다(만들다 → 만드는 게).
Take "-다" off the verb and add "-는 게 어때요?". The final consonant does not matter. A ㄹ final consonant drops (만들다 → 만드는 게).
e: to ride, to take (a bus, boat)
How about going to see a doctor?
tp: "게"는 "것이"가 줄어든 말입니다. 격식 있는 말은 "-는 것이 어떻습니까?"입니다.
"게" is a short form of "것이". The formal form is "-는 것이 어떻습니까?".
더 굳게 권할 때는 "-는 게 좋겠어요"라고 합니다. "병원에 가는 게 좋겠어요."
For a stronger suggestion, say "-는 게 좋겠어요": "병원에 가는 게 좋겠어요." (You'd better go to the hospital.)
명사는 "명사 + 어때요?"입니다. "삼겹살 어때요?"
For nouns, use "noun + 어때요?": "삼겹살 어때요?"
dl: My lower back keeps hurting these days.
How about going to see a doctor?
to not have, to not be there
그럼 아르바이트 사장님께 말하고 하루 쉬는 게 좋겠어요.
Then you'd better tell your part-time job boss and take a day off.
geureom areuba-iteu sajangnimkke malhago haru swineun ge jokesseoyo
sm: "-는 게 어때요?"는 부드럽게 권하는 말입니다.
"-는 게 어때요?" is a soft way to suggest something.
qz: 더 굳게 권하는 말은? -는 게 어때요? / -는 게 좋겠어요

i: Used to tell or ask someone politely to do something. It is like "Please …" in English.
Used to tell or advise someone politely. It is like "Please …" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으세요", 받침이 없으면 "-세요"를 붙입니다. ㄹ 받침은 떨어집니다(만들다 → 만드세요).
With a final consonant add "-으세요"; without one add "-세요". A ㄹ final consonant drops (만들다 → 만드세요).
c: to eat, to drink (polite form of 먹다)
e: Please eat a lot. (Enjoy your meal.)
to eat, to drink (polite form of 먹다)
tp: In English, "please" comes before the verb, but in Korean the end of the verb changes. "Please sit down" = "앉으세요".
In English, "please" comes before the verb, but in Korean the end of the verb changes: "Please sit down" = "앉으세요".
듣는 사람에게 좋은 일을 권할 때 씁니다. 나를 위해 해 달라고 할 때는 "-아/어 주세요"가 더 공손합니다.
Use it to suggest something good for the listener. When you ask someone to do something for you, "-아/어 주세요" is more polite.
먹다, 마시다는 "드세요", 자다는 "주무세요", 있다는 "계세요"입니다.
먹다, 마시다 become "드세요", 자다 becomes "주무세요", and 있다 becomes "계세요".
dl: 여기에 이름을 쓰세요. 그리고 잠시만 기다리세요.
Please write your name here. And please wait a moment.
yeogie ireumeul sseuseyo geurigo jamsiman gidariseyo
sm: "-(으)세요"는 공손하게 시키거나 권하는 말입니다.
"-(으)세요" is a polite way to tell or advise someone to do something.

i: Used when you ask someone to do something for you. It is like "Please … (for me)" or "Could you …?" in English.
Used when you ask someone to do something for you. It is like "Please … (for me)" in English.
m: "-아요/어요" 모양에서 "요"를 떼고 "주세요"를 붙입니다. 명사는 "명사 + 주세요"입니다.
Take "요" off the "-아요/어요" form and add "주세요". For nouns, use "noun + 주세요".
tp: "주다" means "to give". Adding it after a verb means you do something for someone: "도와 주다" = to help (someone).
"주다" means "to give". After a verb, it means doing something for someone: "도와 주다" = to help (someone).
"좀"을 넣으면 더 부드럽습니다. "좀 도와주세요."
Adding "좀" makes it softer: "좀 도와주세요."
더 공손한 말은 "-아/어 주시겠어요?", "-아/어 주실 수 있어요?"입니다.
More polite forms are "-아/어 주시겠어요?" and "-아/어 주실 수 있어요?".
못 알아들었을 때 쓰는 세 마디를 꼭 외웁니다. "다시 말해 주세요", "천천히 말해 주세요", "써 주세요".
Learn these three phrases for when you don't understand: "다시 말해 주세요", "천천히 말해 주세요", "써 주세요".
dl: Professor, I'm sorry, but please say that again.
이 단어를 공책에 세 번 쓰세요.
Write this word in your notebook three times.
i daneoreul gongchaege se beon sseuseyo
Yes, I understand. Please show me once.
to know (알겠습니다 = I understand, got it)
You can write it like this.
sm: "-아/어 주세요"는 나를 위해 해 달라고 부탁하는 말입니다.
"-아/어 주세요" is a request to do something for you.

i: 가장 격식 있게 시키는 말입니다. 안내문, 표지판, 방송, 손님에게 하는 말에서 씁니다.
This is the most formal way to tell someone to do something. It is used in notices, safety signs, announcements and when speaking to customers.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으십시오", 받침이 없으면 "-십시오"를 붙입니다.
With a final consonant add "-으십시오"; without one add "-십시오".
e: Please exit through the emergency exit.
tp: "-십시오"는 [십씨오]로 소리 납니다. 글로는 "-시오"로 끝납니다. "-십시요"라고 쓰면 틀립니다.
"-십시오" is pronounced [십씨오] (sipsio). In writing it ends in "-시오". Writing "-십시요" is wrong.
하지 말라는 말은 "-지 마십시오"입니다. "들어가지 마십시오."
To tell someone not to do something, use "-지 마십시오": "들어가지 마십시오." (Please do not enter.)
학교와 기숙사의 안내문, 지하철 방송은 거의 이 말투입니다. 읽고 알아보는 것이 중요합니다.
Notices at school and in the dorm, and subway announcements, almost always use this style. It is important to read and understand them.
dl: Please be quiet inside the library.
Do not bring food into the reading room.
to have, to hold (가지고 = with, carrying)
Aisha, did you turn off your phone?
sm: "-(으)십시오"는 표지와 방송에서 쓰는 가장 격식 있는 시킴입니다.
"-(으)십시오" is the most formal way to tell someone to do something, used on signs and in announcements.

i: Used to tell someone politely not to do something. It is like "Don't …" or "Please don't …" in English.
Used to tell someone politely not to do something. It is like "Please don't …" in English.
m: 동사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-지 마세요"를 붙입니다. 받침이 있어도 없어도 같습니다.
Take "-다" off the verb and add "-지 마세요". It is the same with or without a final consonant.
e: Don't run. The floor is slippery.
to turn on (a light, a machine)
tp: In English, "don't" comes before the verb, but in Korean "-지 마세요" comes after the verb.
In English, "don't" comes before the verb, but in Korean "-지 마세요" comes after the verb.
"안 가세요?"는 금지가 아니라 질문입니다. 하지 말라고 할 때는 "안"을 쓰지 않습니다.
"안 가세요?" is not a command but a question (Aren't you going?). Don't use "안" to tell someone not to do something.
말투에 따라 모양이 바뀝니다. 친구나 아랫사람에게, 또 급할 때는 "-지 마"(만지지 마!), 보통은 "-지 마세요", 표지와 안내 방송은 "-지 마십시오"입니다.
The form changes with the level of politeness. With friends or younger people, or in an emergency, use "-지 마" (만지지 마!); usually use "-지 마세요"; on signs and in announcements use "-지 마십시오".
pr: 하지 마세요 Please don't do it
들어오지 마세요 Please don't come in
켜지 마세요 Please don't turn it on
dl: 이 커피 머신, 지금 켜도 돼요?
Can I turn on this coffee machine now?
to turn on (a light, a machine)
i keopi meosin, jigeum kyeodo dwaeyo?
아니요, 아직 켜지 마세요. 수리 중이에요.
No, don't turn it on yet. It's being repaired.
to turn on (a light, a machine)
aniyo, ajik kyeoji maseyo suri jungieyo
OK, I understand. Then what shall I do?
to know (알겠습니다 = I understand, got it)
저 상자를 옮기세요. 무거우니까 혼자 들지 마세요.
Move that box. It's heavy, so don't lift it alone.
jeo sangjareul omkkiseyo mugeo-unikka honja deulji maseyo
sm: If you add "-지 마세요" after a verb, it means the same as English "Don't + verb".
If you add "-지 마세요" after a verb, it means the same as "Don't + verb" in English.
qz: 하지 말라는 뜻인 것은? 안 가세요? / 가지 마세요

i: Says what you must not do or what is not allowed. It is like "must not…, can't…" in English.
Says what you must not do or what is not allowed. It is like "must not…, can't…" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으면 안 돼요", 받침이 없거나 ㄹ 받침이면 "-면 안 돼요"를 붙입니다.
After a final consonant (받침) add "-으면 안 돼요"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-면 안 돼요".
e: 수업 중에 휴대폰을 보면 안 돼요.
su-eop junge hyudaeponeul bomyeon an dwaeyo
You must not look at your phone during class.
You must not go in without permission.
tp: "-지 마세요"는 듣는 사람에게 바로 하는 말이고, "-(으)면 안 돼요"는 규칙을 설명하는 말입니다.
"-지 마세요" is said directly to the listener; "-(으)면 안 돼요" explains a rule.
As a question, "-(으)면 안 돼요?" asks for permission, like "Can't I…?": "조금 쉬면 안 돼요?" (Can't I rest a little?)
As a question, "-(으)면 안 돼요?" asks for permission, like "Can't I…?": "조금 쉬면 안 돼요?" (Can't I rest a little?)
The opposite is "-아/어도 돼요" (may, can).
The opposite is "-아/어도 돼요" (may, can).
dl: 사장님, 일할 때 음악을 들어도 돼요?
Boss, can I listen to music while I work?
sajangnim, ilhal ttae eumageul deureodo dwaeyo?
아니요, 이어폰을 끼면 안 돼요. 손님 말을 못 들어요.
No, you must not wear earphones. You can't hear the customers.
to put on, wear (gloves, a ring)
aniyo, ieoponeul kkimyeon an dwaeyo sonnim mareul mot deureoyo
Then what about during break time?
to be fine, to be OK
sm: "-(으)면 안 돼요" means "must not…".
"-(으)면 안 돼요" means "must not…".

i: Shows permission: you may do it. As a question, it asks for permission. It is like "may…, can…, Can I…?" in English.
Shows permission: you may do it. As a question, it asks for permission. It is like "may…, can…, Can I…?" in English.
m: "-아요/어요" 모양에서 "요"를 떼고 "-도 돼요"를 붙입니다.
Take "요" off the "-아요/어요" form and add "-도 돼요".
e: May I go to the restroom?
tp: In English "Can I…?" comes at the start, but Korean "-아/어도 돼요?" comes at the end: "Can I go first?" = "먼저 가도 돼요?"
In English "Can I…?" comes at the start, but Korean "-아/어도 돼요?" comes at the end: "Can I go first?" = "먼저 가도 돼요?"
대답은 "네, 돼요", "네, 그러세요"이고, 안 될 때는 "아니요, 안 돼요", "-(으)면 안 돼요"입니다.
The answer is "네, 돼요" or "네, 그러세요"; if not allowed, "아니요, 안 돼요" or "-(으)면 안 돼요".
"-(으)ㄹ 수 있어요?"는 할 힘이 있는지를 묻고, "-아/어도 돼요?"는 허락을 구합니다.
"-(으)ㄹ 수 있어요?" asks if you are able to; "-아/어도 돼요?" asks for permission.
pr: 가면 안 돼요 must not go
안 해도 돼요 don't have to do
dl: 사장님, 오늘 조금 일찍 가도 돼요?
Boss, may I go home a little early today?
sajangnim, oneul jogeum iljjik gado dwaeyo?
Because I have to go to the bank.
Yes, you may go at five o'clock.
sm: "-아/어도 돼요" means "may…", and "-아/어도 돼요?" means "May I…?".
"-아/어도 돼요" means "may…", and "-아/어도 돼요?" means "May I…?".

i: Says what you must do. It is like "must, have to" in English.
Says what you must do. It is like "must, have to" in English.
m: "-아요/어요" 모양에서 "요"를 떼고 "-야 해요"나 "-야 돼요"를 붙입니다. 둘은 뜻이 같습니다.
Take "요" off the "-아요/어요" form and add "-야 해요" or "-야 돼요". Both mean the same.
c: I have to put them on
e: I have to hand in the assignment by tomorrow.
I have to get up early tomorrow.
to get up, to wake up
약을 하루에 세 번 먹어야 해요.
yageul haru-e se beon meogeoya haeyo
You have to take the medicine three times a day.
You must carry your residence card with you.
tp: English "have to" comes before the verb, but in Korean it is added after the verb: "have to go" = "가야 해요".
English "have to" comes before the verb, but in Korean it is added after the verb: "have to go" = "가야 해요".
말할 때는 "-야 돼요", 글과 격식 있는 말에서는 "-야 합니다"를 많이 씁니다.
In speaking, "-야 돼요" is used a lot; in writing and formal speech, "-야 합니다" is common.
"Don't have to" is "안 -아/어도 돼요", not "-지 않아야 해요".
"Don't have to" is "안 -아/어도 돼요", not "-지 않아야 해요".
pr: 안 가도 돼요 don't have to go
dl: 샘 씨, 실습할 때는 꼭 앞치마를 입어야 해요.
Sam, when you do the practice class, you must wear an apron.
saem ssi, silseupal ttaeneun kkok apchimareul ibeoya haeyo
Do I have to wear a hat too?
네, 음식을 만드니까 모자도 써야 해요.
Yes, we are making food, so you have to wear a hat too.
ne, eumsigeul mandeunikka mojado sseoya haeyo
sm: "-아/어야 해요/돼요" means "have to…, must…".
"-아/어야 해요/돼요" means "have to…, must…".

i: Means doing just that is enough. Used when explaining how to do something. It is like "you just need to…, all you have to do is…" in English.
Means doing just that is enough. Used when explaining how to do something. It is like "you just need to…, all you have to do is…" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으면 돼요", 받침이 없거나 ㄹ 받침이면 "-면 돼요"를 붙입니다.
After a 받침 add "-으면 돼요"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-면 돼요".
c: You just need to press it
You just need to put it in
You just need to do it
e: You just need to press this button.
You only need to write your name here.
By what time should I come?
tp: 어떻게 하는지 물을 때 "어떻게 하면 돼요?"라고 합니다. 일을 배울 때 가장 쓸모 있는 물음입니다.
To ask how to do something, say "어떻게 하면 돼요?" (What should I do? / How do I do it?). It is the most useful question when learning a job.
"-아/어야 돼요"는 꼭 해야 하는 일이고, "-(으)면 돼요"는 그것만 하면 넉넉하다는 뜻입니다.
"-아/어야 돼요" is something you must do; "-(으)면 돼요" means doing only that is enough.
dl: How do I use this washing machine?
먼저 학생증을 대고 시작 버튼을 누르면 돼요.
First tap your student ID card, then just press the start button.
meonjeo haksaengjeungeul daego sijak beoteuneul nureumyeon dwaeyo
And when I want to stop it?
sm: "-(으)면 돼요"는 "you just need to…"입니다.
"-(으)면 돼요" means "you just need to…".
qz: 금지의 뜻인 것은? 가면 돼요 / 가면 안 돼요

i: It is used in two ways: ① "-도록 하세요" is a polite instruction. ② "-도록" means "so that…, so as not to…".
It is used in two ways: ① "-도록 하세요" is a polite instruction. ② "-도록" means "so that…, so as not to…".
m: 동사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-도록"을 붙입니다. 받침과 관계없습니다. 하지 말라는 뜻은 "-지 않도록"입니다.
Take "-다" off the verb and add "-도록". It does not depend on 받침. For "so as not to", use "-지 않도록".
c: Please make sure to do it
so as not to get hurt
so as not to be late
I will make sure to do it
e: Be careful not to get hurt.
Tomorrow, please come by eight o'clock.
I left early so as not to be late.
I will be careful from now on.
tp: 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 시킬 때 많이 씁니다. 대답은 "네, 그렇게 하겠습니다"나 "-도록 하겠습니다"입니다.
Seniors often use it when telling juniors what to do. The answer is "네, 그렇게 하겠습니다" or "-도록 하겠습니다".
학교 공지나 기숙사 규칙에서 "-지 않도록 주의하십시오"를 자주 봅니다. "물건을 잃어버리지 않도록 주의하십시오."
In school notices and dorm rules you often see "-지 않도록 주의하십시오": "물건을 잃어버리지 않도록 주의하십시오." (Be careful not to lose your things.)
dl: Sam, you were late again today.
I'm sorry. I will make sure not to be late again.
다음 수업부터는 십 분 일찍 오도록 하세요.
From the next class, please come ten minutes early.
da-eum su-eopputeoneun sip bun iljjik odorok haseyo
sm: "-도록 하세요" is a polite instruction, and "-지 않도록" means "so as not to…".
"-도록 하세요" is a polite instruction, and "-지 않도록" means "so as not to…".
qz: "Be careful not to get hurt"를 한국어로?

i: Joins two sentences with "and". Used to list two similar actions or qualities side by side.
Joins two sentences with "and". Used to list two similar actions or qualities side by side.
m: 동사나 형용사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-고"를 붙입니다. 받침과 관계없습니다. 명사는 "(이)고"입니다.
Take "-다" off a verb or adjective and add "-고". It does not depend on 받침. For nouns, use "(이)고".
e: This restaurant is cheap and tasty.
The room is big and clean.
I study business administration, and my younger sibling works.
샘 씨는 미국 사람이고 민하 씨는 한국 사람이에요.
saem ssineun miguk saramigo minha ssineun han-guk saramieyo
Sam is American, and Minha is Korean.
tp: 명사와 명사는 "하고"로, 문장과 문장은 "-고"로 잇습니다. "밥하고 김치", "싸고 맛있어요".
Join a noun and a noun with "하고", and a sentence and a sentence with "-고": "밥하고 김치", "싸고 맛있어요".
지난 일도 앞은 그대로 두고 끝만 바꿉니다. "싸고 맛있었어요."
For the past, keep the first part as it is and change only the end: "싸고 맛있었어요."
문장을 끊어서 말하려면 "그리고"를 씁니다. "싸요. 그리고 맛있어요."
To split it into two sentences, use "그리고": "싸요. 그리고 맛있어요."
dl: The room is spacious and clean.
Is it close to the school?
sm: "-고" joins sentences with "and".
"-고" joins sentences with "and".

i: Means you finish the first action and then do the next one. It is like "…and then…, after…ing" in English.
Means you finish the first action and then do the next one. It is like "…and then…, after…ing" in English.
m: 동사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-고"나 "-고 나서"를 붙입니다. "-고 나서"는 앞의 일이 다 끝났다는 뜻이 더 뚜렷합니다.
Take "-다" off the verb and add "-고" or "-고 나서". "-고 나서" makes it clearer that the first action is fully finished.
e: I finish my assignment and then rest.
I wash my hands and then eat.
Turn off the computer and then go out.
What did you do after dinner?
tp: 순서를 설명할 때 아주 많이 씁니다. "신청서를 쓰고, 사진을 붙이고, 학과 사무실에 냅니다."
It is used very often when explaining steps: "신청서를 쓰고, 사진을 붙이고, 학과 사무실에 냅니다." (Write the application, attach a photo, and hand it in at the department office.)
입는 동사와 타는 동사는 "-고"를 씁니다. "모자를 쓰고 나가요", "버스를 타고 가요".
Verbs of wearing and riding use "-고": "모자를 쓰고 나가요" (put on a hat and go out), "버스를 타고 가요" (go by bus).
"가다, 오다, 일어나다, 앉다, 만나다" 뒤에서는 "-고"가 아니라 "-아서/어서"를 씁니다. 이것은 다음 묶음에서 배웁니다.
After "가다, 오다, 일어나다, 앉다, 만나다", use "-아서/어서", not "-고". You will learn this in the next set.
dl: What do you do when work is finished?
커피 머신을 끄고 나서 테이블을 닦습니다.
I turn off the coffee machine and then wipe the tables.
keopi meosineul kkeugo naseo te-ibeureul dakseumnida
I put away the cups and then go to the dorm.
to tidy up, to put away
sm: "-고", "-고 나서"는 일의 순서를 나타냅니다.
"-고" and "-고 나서" show the order of actions.
qz: "-고 나서"와 뜻이 가까운 것은? -기 전에 / -(으)ㄴ 후에
I go by bus (take the bus and go)

i: 앞의 일과 뒤의 일이 이어져 있을 때 씁니다. 앞의 일을 한 그곳에서, 또는 그 상태로 뒤의 일을 합니다.
Used when the first action and the next action are linked. You do the next action in the place of the first action, or in that state.
m: "-아요/어요" 모양에서 "요"를 떼고 "서"를 붙입니다. 가다 → 가서, 만나다 → 만나서, 만들다 → 만들어서.
Take "요" off the "-아요/어요" form and add "서": 가다 → 가서, 만나다 → 만나서, 만들다 → 만들어서.
e: I went to the market and bought apples.
I met a friend and we watched a movie.
I bought gimbap and ate it in the park.
tp: "시장에 가서 샀어요"는 시장에서 샀다는 뜻입니다. "시장에 가고 샀어요"라고 하면 두 일이 따로인 것처럼 들립니다.
"시장에 가서 샀어요" means you bought it at the market. If you say "시장에 가고 샀어요", it sounds like two separate actions.
지난 일이어도 "-았/었-"을 넣지 않습니다. "갔어서"는 틀리고 "가서"가 맞습니다.
Even for the past, do not add "-았/었-". "갔어서" is wrong; "가서" is right.
dl: What did you do on the weekend?
I went to Seoul and met a friend.
What did you do after you met?
We went to a Nepali restaurant and ate.
sm: "-아서/어서"는 이어진 두 일을 차례로 말합니다.
"-아서/어서" tells two linked actions in order.

i: Means "before doing…". It is like "before" in English.
Means "before doing…". It is like "before" in English.
m: 동사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-기 전에"를 붙입니다. 명사는 "명사 + 전에"입니다.
Take "-다" off the verb and add "-기 전에". For nouns, use "noun + 전에".
e: I wash my hands before eating.
Turn off your phone before class starts.
I learned Korean before I came to Korea.
to eat, to drink (polite form of 먹다)
tp: The order is the opposite of English "before + verb": "before eating" = "먹기 전에".
The order is the opposite of English "before + verb": "before eating" = "먹기 전에".
지난 일이어도 "-기 전에" 앞은 바꾸지 않습니다. "왔기 전에"는 틀립니다.
Even for the past, do not change the part before "-기 전에". "왔기 전에" is wrong.
시간에는 "시간 + 전에"를 씁니다. "한 시간 전에", "이 년 전에".
With time, use "time + 전에": "한 시간 전에" (an hour ago), "이 년 전에" (two years ago).
dl: 시험을 시작하기 전에 뭘 해야 해요?
What do you have to do before the exam starts?
siheomeul sijakagi jeone mwol haeya haeyo?
We have to put our student ID card on the desk.
Right. And before the exam ends?
We have to check our names again.
sm: "Verb + -기 전에" means "before + verb".
"Verb + -기 전에" means "before + verb".

i: Means "after doing…". It is like "after" in English.
Means "after doing…". It is like "after" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-은 후에", 받침이 없으면 "-ㄴ 후에"를 붙입니다. "-(으)ㄴ 다음에", "-(으)ㄴ 뒤에"도 같은 뜻입니다. 명사는 "명사 + 후에"입니다.
After a 받침 add "-은 후에"; with no 받침 add "-ㄴ 후에". "-(으)ㄴ 다음에" and "-(으)ㄴ 뒤에" mean the same. For nouns, use "noun + 후에".
e: Let's meet after class is over.
Take the medicine after you eat.
to eat, to drink (polite form of 먹다)
한국에 온 후에 한국 친구가 많이 생겼어요.
han-guge on hu-e han-guk chin-guga mani saenggyeosseoyo
After I came to Korea, I made many Korean friends.
What do you do after class?
tp: The order is the opposite of English "after + verb": "after eating" = "먹은 후에".
The order is the opposite of English "after + verb": "after eating" = "먹은 후에".
시간에는 "시간 + 후에"를 씁니다. "삼십 분 후에 오세요."
With time, use "time + 후에": "삼십 분 후에 오세요." (Please come in 30 minutes.)
약 봉투에서 "식후 30분"은 "밥을 먹은 후 30분"이라는 뜻입니다.
On a medicine bag, "식후 30분" means "30 minutes after eating".
dl: When do I take this medicine?
식사한 후에 드세요. 하루에 세 번입니다.
Take it after meals. It's three times a day.
to eat, to drink (polite form of 먹다)
siksahan hu-e deuseyo haru-e se beonimnida
Do I take it right after eating?
to eat, to drink (polite form of 먹다)
sm: "Verb + -(으)ㄴ 후에" means "after + verb".
"Verb + -(으)ㄴ 후에" means "after + verb".

i: Means doing two things at the same time. It is like "while …ing" in English.
Means doing two things at the same time. It is like "while …ing" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으면서", 받침이 없거나 ㄹ 받침이면 "-면서"를 붙입니다.
After a 받침 add "-으면서"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-면서".
e: I study while listening to music.
I learned Korean while working part-time.
Looking at your phone while walking is dangerous.
tp: 두 일을 하는 사람이 같아야 합니다. 사람이 다르면 "-는 동안"을 씁니다.
The same person must do both actions. If the people are different, use "-는 동안".
더 중요한 일을 뒤에 말합니다. "운전하면서 전화하지 마세요."
Say the more important action last: "운전하면서 전화하지 마세요." (Don't talk on the phone while driving.)
듣다는 "들으면서", 걷다는 "걸으면서"가 됩니다(ㄷ 불규칙).
듣다 becomes "들으면서" and 걷다 becomes "걸으면서" (ㄷ irregular).
dl: Isn't it hard to study while working?
sm: "-(으)면서"는 한 사람이 두 일을 함께 한다는 뜻입니다.
"-(으)면서" means one person does two things at the same time.

i: Means during the time something is going on. It is like "while, during" in English.
Means during the time something is going on. It is like "while, during" in English.
m: 동사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-는 동안"을 붙입니다. ㄹ 받침은 떨어집니다(돌다 → 도는 동안). 명사는 "명사 + 동안"입니다.
Take "-다" off the verb and add "-는 동안". A ㄹ 받침 drops (돌다 → 도는 동안). For nouns, use "noun + 동안".
e: 룸메이트가 자는 동안 조용히 해 주세요.
rumme-iteuga janeun dongan joyonghi hae juseyo
Please be quiet while my roommate is sleeping.
I drank coffee while I waited.
I lived in Jeonju for three years.
제가 없는 동안 무슨 일 있었어요?
jega eomneun dongan museun il isseosseoyo?
Did anything happen while I was away?
to not have, to not be there
tp: 앞과 뒤의 주어가 달라도 됩니다. "제가 청소하는 동안 아이샤 씨가 요리했어요."
The subjects of the two parts can be different: "제가 청소하는 동안 아이샤 씨가 요리했어요." (While I cleaned, Aisha cooked.)
걸린 시간을 말할 때 "시간 + 동안"을 씁니다. "얼마 동안 한국에 있었어요?"
To say how long something took, use "time + 동안": "얼마 동안 한국에 있었어요?" (How long were you in Korea?)
시험 규칙에 자주 나옵니다. "시험을 보는 동안 휴대폰을 끄십시오."
It often appears in exam rules: "시험을 보는 동안 휴대폰을 끄십시오." (Turn off your phone while taking the exam.)
dl: Please wait here while the professor is in a meeting.
Yes. How long is the meeting?
sm: "-는 동안"은 "while…", "시간 + 동안"은 "for (a time)"입니다.
"-는 동안" means "while…", and "time + 동안" means "for (a time)".

i: Used when the first and second parts contrast. It is like "but" in English.
Used when the first and second parts contrast. It is like "but" in English.
m: 동사나 형용사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-지만"을 붙입니다. 받침과 관계없습니다. 지난 일은 "-았/었지만"입니다.
Take "-다" off a verb or adjective and add "-지만". It does not depend on 받침. For the past, use "-았/었지만".
e: Studying is hard, but it's fun.
Kimchi is spicy, but it's tasty.
Korean is difficult, but I study hard.
I took medicine, but it still hurts.
tp: In English "but" comes at the start of the second part, but "-지만" is added to the end of the first part.
In English "but" comes at the start of the second part, but "-지만" is added to the end of the first part.
문장을 끊으면 "하지만"이나 "그렇지만"을 씁니다. "힘들어요. 하지만 재미있어요."
To split it into two sentences, use "하지만" or "그렇지만": "힘들어요. 하지만 재미있어요."
말을 꺼낼 때 "죄송하지만", "실례지만"으로 시작하면 공손합니다.
Starting with "죄송하지만" or "실례지만" (Excuse me, but…) sounds polite.
dl: I miss my family, but I'm okay.
to see (보고 싶다 = to miss, want to see)
to be fine, to be OK
It was hard at first, but now I'm used to it.
sm: "-지만" means "but" and is added to the end of the first part.
"-지만" means "but" and is added to the end of the first part.

i: Used to give the background situation first, before what you say next. It is also used for contrast (but). There is no exact match in English.
Used to give the background situation first, before what you say next. It is also used for contrast (but). There is no exact match in English.
m: 동사와 "있다/없다"에는 "-는데", 형용사에는 받침이 있으면 "-은데", 없으면 "-ㄴ데", 명사에는 "인데", 지난 일에는 "-았/었는데"를 붙입니다.
Add "-는데" to verbs and "있다/없다"; to adjectives add "-은데" after a 받침 and "-ㄴ데" with no 받침; to nouns add "인데"; for the past add "-았/었는데".
c: to not have, to not be there
e: I'm busy now, so let's talk later.
It's raining. Do you have an umbrella?
I worked hard, but it didn't go well.
This is Sam. Is the professor there?
tp: 부탁하거나 물어보기 전에 사정을 말할 때 가장 많이 씁니다. "길을 잘 모르는데 좀 가르쳐 주세요."
It is used most when you explain the situation before asking for help or asking a question: "길을 잘 모르는데 좀 가르쳐 주세요." (I don't know the way well. Could you tell me?)
문장을 "-는데요"로 끝내면 뒷말을 줄인 부드러운 대답이 됩니다. "지금 없는데요."
Ending a sentence with "-는데요" makes a soft answer that leaves the rest unsaid: "지금 없는데요." (He's not here right now…)
dl: 교수님, 드릴 말씀이 있는데 시간 괜찮으세요?
Professor, I have something to tell you. Do you have time?
to be fine, to be OK
gyosunim, deuril malsseumi inneunde sigan gwaenchaneuseyo?
다음 주에 병원에 가야 하는데 수업을 하루 빠져도 될까요?
I have to go to the hospital next week. Could I miss class for one day?
da-eum ju-e byeongwone gaya haneunde su-eobeul haru ppajeodo doelkkayo?
sm: "-는데/(으)ㄴ데"는 뒷말의 바탕이 되는 사정을 먼저 말합니다.
"-는데/(으)ㄴ데" first gives the background situation for what comes next.

i: Used when choosing one of two actions. It is like "or" in English.
Used when choosing one of two actions. It is like "or" in English.
m: 동사나 형용사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-거나"를 붙입니다. 받침과 관계없습니다.
Take "-다" off a verb or adjective and add "-거나". It does not depend on 받침.
e: On weekends I rest or meet friends.
In the evening I watch TV or listen to music.
If you are sick or get hurt, tell us right away.
If you don't know something, ask or look it up in a dictionary.
tp: 명사는 "(이)나", 동사와 형용사는 "-거나"입니다. "커피나 차", "마시거나 먹거나".
Nouns use "(이)나", and verbs and adjectives use "-거나": "커피나 차" (coffee or tea), "마시거나 먹거나" (drink or eat).
English "or" stands alone in the middle, but "-거나" is attached to the first verb.
English "or" stands alone in the middle, but "-거나" is attached to the first verb.
문장을 끊으면 "아니면"이나 "또는"을 씁니다.
To split it into two sentences, use "아니면" or "또는".
dl: What do you usually do on your day off?
I sleep at home or do the laundry.
Sometimes I go to the market or meet friends.
sm: "Verb + -거나" means "verb + or".
"Verb + -거나" means "verb + or".
qz: If you are sick or get hurt

i: Used to give a reason. It is like "because…, so…" in English.
Used to give a reason. It is like "because…, so…" in English.
m: "-아요/어요" 모양에서 "요"를 떼고 "서"를 붙입니다. 명사는 "(이)라서"입니다.
Take "요" off the "-아요/어요" form and add "서". For nouns, use "(이)라서".
e: I couldn't go because I was sick.
I was late because of the traffic.
tp: English "because" comes before the reason, but Korean adds "-아서/어서" to the end of the reason part. The reason comes first, and the result comes after.
English "because" comes before the reason, but Korean adds "-아서/어서" to the end of the reason part. The reason comes first, and the result comes after.
뒤에 시키는 말(-세요)이나 같이 하자는 말(-ㅂ시다)이 올 수 없습니다. 그때는 "-(으)니까"를 씁니다. "추워서 문을 닫으세요"는 틀립니다.
The second part cannot be an order (-세요) or a suggestion (-ㅂ시다). In that case use "-(으)니까". "추워서 문을 닫으세요" is wrong.
고맙다, 미안하다, 죄송하다, 반갑다 앞에는 늘 "-아서/어서"를 씁니다. "만나서 반갑습니다."
Before 고맙다, 미안하다, 죄송하다, 반갑다, always use "-아서/어서": "만나서 반갑습니다." (Nice to meet you.)
dl: I'm sorry. I missed the bus, so I was late.
From next time, please come earlier.
Yes, I'm sorry to have worried you.
sm: "-아서/어서"는 까닭을 나타내고, 뒤에 시키는 말은 올 수 없습니다.
"-아서/어서" shows a reason, and the second part cannot be an order.

i: Used to give a reason. Used when the second part is an order or a suggestion. It is like "because…, since…" in English.
Used to give a reason. Used when the second part is an order or a suggestion. It is like "because…, since…" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으니까", 받침이 없거나 ㄹ 받침이면 "-니까"를 붙입니다. ㄹ 받침은 떨어집니다(멀다 → 머니까). 지난 일은 "-았/었으니까"입니다.
After a 받침 add "-으니까"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-니까". A ㄹ 받침 drops (멀다 → 머니까). For the past, use "-았/었으니까".
c: to not have, to not be there
e: We don't have time, so let's go quickly.
to not have, to not be there
It's hot, so don't touch it.
It's raining, so take an umbrella with you.
tp: 안전을 알리는 말은 거의 "-(으)니까 + -(으)세요/-지 마세요" 모양입니다.
Safety warnings are almost always in the form "-(으)니까 + -(으)세요/-지 마세요".
윗사람에게 내 사정을 말할 때 "-(으)니까"를 쓰면 따지는 것처럼 들릴 수 있습니다. "아프니까 못 가요"보다 "아파서 못 가요"가 부드럽습니다.
When you give your own reason to a senior, "-(으)니까" can sound like you are arguing. "아파서 못 가요" is softer than "아프니까 못 가요".
dl: 이 냄비는 뜨거우니까 꼭 장갑을 끼세요.
This pot is hot, so be sure to wear gloves.
to put on, wear (gloves, a ring)
i naembineun tteugeo-unikka kkok janggabeul kkiseyo
Yes, I understand. Should I wear an apron too?
Yes, oil splashes, so wear an apron too.
sm: 시키는 말 앞에서 까닭을 말할 때는 "-(으)니까"를 씁니다.
When you give a reason before an order, use "-(으)니까".
qz: 맞는 것은? 추워서 문을 닫으세요 / 추우니까 문을 닫으세요

i: Used to state a reason clearly. Often used in writing, reports and presentations. It is like "because, due to" in English.
Used to state a reason clearly. Often used in writing, reports and presentations. It is like "because, due to" in English.
m: 동사나 형용사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-기 때문에"를 붙입니다. 지난 일은 "-았/었기 때문에", 명사는 "명사 + 때문에"입니다.
Take "-다" off and add "-기 때문에". For the past, use "-았/었기 때문에"; for nouns, use "noun + 때문에".
e: Because it is raining, the festival was canceled.
Because I have a lot of assignments, I'm going to the library.
I went to the hospital because of a cold.
버스가 고장 났기 때문에 수업에 늦었습니다.
beoseuga gojang natki ttaemune su-eobe neujeotseumnida
Because the bus broke down, I was late for class.
tp: 뒤에 시키는 말이나 같이 하자는 말이 올 수 없습니다.
The second part cannot be an order or a suggestion.
"명사 + 때문에"는 흔히 좋지 않은 일의 까닭입니다. 좋은 일의 까닭은 "덕분에"입니다.
"Noun + 때문에" is usually the cause of something bad. For the cause of something good, use "덕분에".
까닭을 물을 때 "왜요?", "무엇 때문에요?"라고 하고, 대답은 "~기 때문입니다"로 끝낼 수 있습니다.
To ask for a reason, say "왜요?" or "무엇 때문에요?", and you can end the answer with "~기 때문입니다".
dl: 샘 씨, 과제를 왜 늦게 냈습니까?
Sam, why did you hand in the assignment late?
saem ssi, gwajereul wae neutke naetseumnikka?
It's because my laptop broke down yesterday.
to be fine, to be OK
Yes, I had it repaired, so there is no problem.
sm: "-기 때문에"는 까닭을 뚜렷하게 밝히는 격식 있는 말입니다.
"-기 때문에" is a formal way to state a reason clearly.
qz: 좋은 일의 까닭에 쓰는 말은? 때문에 / 덕분에

i: Gives a condition. It is like "if" in English.
Gives a condition. It is like "if" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으면", 받침이 없거나 ㄹ 받침이면 "-면"을 붙입니다. 명사는 "(이)면"입니다.
After a 받침 add "-으면"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-면". For nouns, use "(이)면".
e: If you have time, let's go together.
If it hurts, don't put up with it. Tell us.
to put up with, hold back
I'll call you when class is over.
tp: English "if" comes at the start of the condition, but "-(으)면" is added to its end: "if you don't know" = "모르면".
English "if" comes at the start of the condition, but "-(으)면" is added to its end: "if you don't know" = "모르면".
It is also used for things that will surely happen. Then it means "when": "봄이 되면 따뜻해져요." (When spring comes, it gets warm.)
It is also used for things that will surely happen. Then it means "when": "봄이 되면 따뜻해져요." (When spring comes, it gets warm.)
앞에 "만약, 만일, 혹시"를 넣어서 조건임을 뚜렷하게 할 수 있습니다. "혹시 늦으면 연락하세요."
You can add "만약, 만일, 혹시" in front to make the condition clear: "혹시 늦으면 연락하세요." (If you are late, please contact me.)
dl: What do you do if there is a fire in the dorm?
to break out (불이 나다 = a fire breaks out)
I go outside right away and call 119.
맞아요. 계단이 어두우면 휴대폰 불을 켜세요.
Right. If the stairs are dark, turn on your phone's light.
majayo gedani eodu-umyeon hyudaepon bureul kyeoseyo
sm: "-(으)면" means "if…" and is added to the end of the condition.
"-(으)면" means "if…" and is added to the end of the condition.

i: Means "if you want to…". Used to tell how to reach a goal. It is like "if you want to…, (in order) to…" in English.
Means "if you want to…". Used to tell how to reach a goal. It is like "if you want to…, (in order) to…" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으려면", 받침이 없거나 ㄹ 받침이면 "-려면"을 붙입니다. 뒤에는 "-아/어야 해요", "-(으)세요", "-(으)면 돼요"가 옵니다.
After a 받침 add "-으려면"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-려면". After it comes "-아/어야 해요", "-(으)세요" or "-(으)면 돼요".
c: if you want to be good at
e: To go to Korea, you have to take a test.
To open a bank account, you need your residence card.
시청에 가려면 몇 번 버스를 타야 돼요?
sicheonge garyeomyeon myeot beon beoseureul taya dwaeyo?
Which bus do I have to take to go to City Hall?
to ride, to take (a bus, boat)
If you want to be good at Korean, practice every day.
to do well, to be good at
tp: 길을 묻거나 절차를 물을 때 가장 쓸모 있는 문형입니다. "~(으)려면 어떻게 해야 돼요?"
It is the most useful pattern for asking the way or asking about procedures: "~(으)려면 어떻게 해야 돼요?" (What do I have to do to…?)
pr: 가려면 if you want to go
dl: 체류 기간을 연장하려면 어떻게 해야 돼요?
What do I have to do to extend my period of stay?
cheryu giganeul yeonjangharyeomyeon eotteoke haeya dwaeyo?
You have to apply at the immigration office.
What do I need to apply?
You need your passport, residence card and certificate of enrollment.
sm: "-(으)려면" means "if you want to…", and the way to do it comes after.
"-(으)려면" means "if you want to…", and the way to do it comes after.
qz: "What do I have to do to…?"를 한국어로?

i: Tells the purpose of going or coming. It is like "go/come to + verb" (go to eat) in English.
Tells the purpose of going or coming. It is like "go/come to + verb" (go to eat) in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으러", 받침이 없거나 ㄹ 받침이면 "-러"를 붙이고, 뒤에 "가다, 오다, 다니다"를 씁니다.
After a 받침 add "-으러"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-러", then use "가다, 오다, 다니다".
c: go out (to have fun), go on a trip
e: I came to Korea to study.
Come over and visit on the weekend.
I'm going to the bank to take out money.
tp: In English "go" comes first (go to eat), but in Korean "가요" comes at the end (먹으러 가요).
In English "go" comes first (go to eat), but in Korean "가요" comes at the end (먹으러 가요).
뒤에는 움직이는 동사(가다, 오다, 다니다, 나가다, 들어오다)만 옵니다. 다른 동사가 오면 "-(으)려고"를 씁니다.
Only verbs of movement (가다, 오다, 다니다, 나가다, 들어오다) can come after it. With other verbs, use "-(으)려고".
가는 곳은 "에"로 말합니다. "식당에 밥 먹으러 가요."
Say the place you go to with "에": "식당에 밥 먹으러 가요." (I'm going to a restaurant to eat.)
dl: I'm going to the post office to send a package.
저도 편지를 부치러 가야 하는데 같이 가요.
I have to go mail a letter too, so let's go together.
jeodo pyeonjireul buchireo gaya haneunde gachi gayo
sm: "-(으)러 가요/와요" means "go/come to + verb".
"-(으)러 가요/와요" means "go/come to + verb".
qz: "-(으)러" 뒤에 올 수 있는 것은? 가다 / 먹다

i: Tells the purpose of an action. It is like "to…, in order to…" in English.
Tells the purpose of an action. It is like "to…, in order to…" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-으려고", 받침이 없거나 ㄹ 받침이면 "-려고"를 붙입니다. 뒤에 어떤 동사나 올 수 있습니다.
After a 받침 add "-으려고"; with no 받침 or with ㄹ 받침 add "-려고". Any verb can come after it.
e: I came to open a bank account.
I'm saving money to send to my family.
I'm learning Korean to study at a Korean university.
I went to bed early so I could get up early.
to get up, to wake up
tp: In English you usually say the action first and then the purpose after "to, in order to", but in Korean the purpose comes first and the action comes after.
In English you usually say the action first and then the purpose after "to, in order to", but in Korean the purpose comes first and the action comes after.
뒤에 시키는 말이나 같이 하자는 말은 잘 쓰지 않습니다. 그때는 "-(으)려면"을 씁니다.
Orders and suggestions are not usually used after it. In that case, use "-(으)려면".
창구에서 온 까닭을 말할 때 "~(으)려고 왔어요", "~(으)려고요"라고 합니다.
At a counter, to say why you came, say "~(으)려고 왔어요" or "~(으)려고요".
dl: How can I help you? (Why did you come?)
I came to pay my tuition.
Please give me your bankbook and ID card.
sm: "-(으)려고" means "in order to…", and the purpose is said first.
"-(으)려고" means "in order to…", and the purpose is said first.

i: Used to add the reason for what you just said. It tells something the listener does not know. It feels like "…, you see" or "because…" in English.
Used to add the reason for what you just said. It tells something the listener does not know. It feels like "…, you see" or "because…" in English.
m: 동사나 형용사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-거든요"를 붙입니다. 지난 일은 "-았/었거든요", 명사는 "(이)거든요"입니다.
Take "-다" off and add "-거든요". For the past, use "-았/었거든요"; for nouns, use "(이)거든요".
c: because it's (my) first time, you see
e: I'm leaving early today. I have plans, you see.
I won't eat. I ate a little while ago, you see.
I'm not sure. It's my first time here, you see.
I'm a little tired these days. I have a lot of assignments, you see.
tp: 까닭이 뒤에 옵니다. "-아서/어서"와 순서가 반대입니다. "약속이 있어서 일찍 가요" = "일찍 가요. 약속이 있거든요."
The reason comes after. The order is the opposite of "-아서/어서": "약속이 있어서 일찍 가요" = "일찍 가요. 약속이 있거든요."
[거든뇨]로 소리 납니다.
It is pronounced [거든뇨].
dl: 샘 씨, 오늘 동아리 모임에 안 가요?
Sam, aren't you going to the club meeting today?
saem ssi, oneul dongari mo-ime an gayo?
네, 못 가요. 몸이 좀 안 좋거든요.
No, I can't go. I'm not feeling well, you see.
(몸이 안 좋다 = to not feel well)
ne, mot gayo momi jom an jokeodeunyo
I've had a headache since yesterday, you see.
sm: "-거든요"는 앞말의 까닭을 뒤에서 덧붙입니다.
"-거든요" adds the reason for what was said before, after it.
qz: 격식 있는 자리에서 쓰는 말은? -거든요 / -기 때문입니다

i: 좋은 결과가 생긴 까닭을 고마워하며 말할 때 씁니다. 영어 "thanks to…"입니다.
Used to give the reason for a good result, with thanks. It is like "thanks to…" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-은 덕분에", 받침이 없으면 "-ㄴ 덕분에"를 붙입니다. 명사는 "명사 + 덕분에"입니다.
After a 받침 add "-은 덕분에"; with no 받침 add "-ㄴ 덕분에". For nouns, use "noun + 덕분에".
e: Thanks to your help, we finished quickly.
Thanks to the professor, I learned Korean well.
I've been well, thanks to you.
Thanks to practicing hard, I passed the test.
tp: 좋은 일에만 씁니다. 나쁜 일에는 "때문에"나 "-는 바람에"를 씁니다.
Use it only for good things. For bad things, use "때문에" or "-는 바람에".
"덕분에 잘 지냈어요", "덕분입니다"는 안부 인사에 대한 대답으로 굳어 있습니다.
"덕분에 잘 지냈어요" and "덕분입니다" are set phrases used to answer "How have you been?"
dl: 샘 씨, 이번 시험에서 백 점을 받았어요. 잘했어요.
Sam, you got 100 points on this exam. Well done.
saem ssi, ibeon siheomeseo baek jeomeul badasseoyo jalhaesseoyo
감사합니다. 진하 씨가 잘 가르쳐 준 덕분입니다.
Thank you. It's thanks to Jinha teaching me well.
to give (-아/어 주다 = do for someone)
gamsahamnida jinha ssiga jal gareucheo jun deokpunimnida
Keep working hard from now on too.
sm: "덕분에"는 좋은 결과의 까닭을 고마워하며 말합니다.
"덕분에" gives the reason for a good result, with thanks.
qz: 좋은 일의 까닭에 쓰는 말은? 때문에 / 덕분에

i: A verb describes a noun. It shows something happening now or done regularly. It is like "the … who/that …" in English.
A verb describes a noun. It shows something happening now or done regularly. It is like "the … who/that …" in English.
m: 동사와 "있다/없다"의 "-다"를 떼고 "-는"을 붙인 뒤 명사를 놓습니다. ㄹ 받침은 떨어집니다(살다 → 사는).
Take "-다" off verbs and "있다/없다", add "-는", then put the noun. A ㄹ 받침 drops (살다 → 사는).
e: What is the work you are doing now?
The person standing over there is the teaching assistant.
The place where I live is Jeonju.
If there is something you don't know, ask.
tp: In English the describing part comes after the noun (a person who works), but in Korean it comes before (일하는 사람). There is no separate word for "who, that".
In English the describing part comes after the noun (a person who works), but in Korean it comes before (일하는 사람). There is no separate word for "who, that".
"맛있다, 재미있다"도 "있다"로 끝나서 "-는"을 씁니다. "맛있는 음식", "재미없는 영화".
"맛있다, 재미있다" also end in "있다", so they use "-는": "맛있는 음식" (tasty food), "재미없는 영화" (a boring movie).
dl: 저기 모자를 쓰고 있는 사람이 누구예요?
Who is the person wearing a hat over there?
jeogi mojareul sseugo inneun sarami nuguyeyo?
That's Aisha, who studies with me.
What part-time job does Aisha do?
She makes coffee at a cafe.
sm: "Verb + -는 + noun" means "noun + who/that + verb".
"Verb + -는 + noun" means "noun + who/that + verb".

i: 두 가지로 씁니다. ① 형용사로 명사를 꾸밉니다(큰 상자). ② 동사에 붙으면 지난 일을 나타냅니다(어제 만난 사람).
It is used in two ways: ① An adjective describes a noun (큰 상자, a big box). ② Added to a verb, it shows the past (어제 만난 사람, the person I met yesterday).
m: 받침이 있으면 "-은", 받침이 없으면 "-ㄴ"을 붙입니다. ㄹ 받침은 떨어지고(길다 → 긴), ㅂ 불규칙은 "-운"이 됩니다(덥다 → 더운).
After a 받침 add "-은"; with no 받침 add "-ㄴ". A ㄹ 받침 drops (길다 → 긴), and ㅂ irregular becomes "-운" (덥다 → 더운).
e: Who is the person you met yesterday?
The shoes I bought last week are small.
tp: As in English "big box", the adjective comes before the noun, but in Korean the adjective changes its form (크다 → 큰 상자).
As in English "big box", the adjective comes before the noun, but in Korean the adjective changes its form (크다 → 큰 상자).
It is the same "-(으)ㄴ", but with adjectives it is a present quality, and with verbs it is the past: "바쁜 사람" (a busy person), "온 사람" (a person who came).
It is the same "-(으)ㄴ", but with adjectives it is a present quality, and with verbs it is the past: "바쁜 사람" (a busy person), "온 사람" (a person who came).
pr: 가는 사람 a person who is going
간 사람 a person who went
dl: 샘 씨, 어제 빌린 책은 어디에 있어요?
Sam, where are the books you borrowed yesterday?
saem ssi, eoje billin chaegeun eodie isseoyo?
I put them in that big box.
Did you put the small ones in too?
아니요, 작은 것은 파란 상자에 넣었습니다.
No, I put the small ones in the blue box.
aniyo, jageun geoseun paran sangja-e neo-eotseumnida
sm: 형용사 + "-(으)ㄴ"은 꾸밈, 동사 + "-(으)ㄴ"은 지난 일입니다.
Adjective + "-(으)ㄴ" describes; verb + "-(으)ㄴ" shows the past.

i: Describes a noun with something you will do or that has not happened yet. It is like "… to do, … that (I) will…" in English.
Describes a noun with something you will do or that has not happened yet. It is like "… to do, … that (I) will…" in English.
m: 받침이 있으면 "-을", 받침이 없으면 "-ㄹ"을 붙입니다. ㄹ 받침은 그대로 둡니다(만들다 → 만들).
After a 받침 add "-을"; with no 받침 add "-ㄹ". A ㄹ 받침 stays as it is (만들다 → 만들).
e: I have a lot of work to do tomorrow.
I have no time to rest.
to not have, to not be there
I have something to tell you. (humble)
tp: 세 가지를 견주어 보세요. 하는 일(work I'm doing), 한 일(work I did), 할 일(work I will do).
Compare the three forms: 하는 일 (work I'm doing), 한 일 (work I did), 할 일 (work I will do).
"-(으)ㄹ" 뒤의 ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ, ㅅ, ㅈ은 된소리가 됩니다. 갈 곳 [갈 꼳], 먹을 것 [머글 껃].
After "-(으)ㄹ", ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ, ㅅ, ㅈ become tense sounds: 갈 곳 [갈 꼳], 먹을 것 [머글 껃].
"-(으)ㄹ 때, -(으)ㄹ 수 있다, -(으)ㄹ 거예요"가 모두 이 모양에서 나왔습니다.
"-(으)ㄹ 때, -(으)ㄹ 수 있다, -(으)ㄹ 거예요" all come from this form.
dl: I'll tell you the work to do today.
오전에 씻을 컵이 오십 개 있어요.
This morning there are 50 cups to wash.
ojeone ssiseul keobi osip gae isseoyo
I understand. Is there work to do in the afternoon too?
to know (알겠습니다 = I understand, got it)
sm: "Verb + -(으)ㄹ + noun" means "noun + to + verb" (work to do).
"Verb + -(으)ㄹ + noun" means "noun + to + verb" (work to do).
qz: "work I did"는? 한 일 / 할 일

i: Lets a verb be used like a noun. It is like "…ing" (cooking) or "to…" in English.
Lets a verb be used like a noun. It is like "…ing" (cooking) or "to…" in English.
m: 동사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-는 것"을 붙입니다. 말할 때는 "것이 → 게", "것을 → 걸", "것은 → 건"으로 줄입니다.
Take "-다" off the verb and add "-는 것". In speech, shorten "것이 → 게", "것을 → 걸", "것은 → 건".
tp: Like English "-ing", "-는 것" comes after the verb: "learning" = "배우는 것".
Like English "-ing", "-는 것" comes after the verb: "learning" = "배우는 것".
"좋아하다, 싫어하다, 잘하다, 못하다" 앞에서 많이 씁니다. "운전하는 것을 잘해요."
It is often used before "좋아하다, 싫어하다, 잘하다, 못하다": "운전하는 것을 잘해요." (I'm good at driving.)
"것" also means "thing, one": "이것, 그것, 먹을 것, 큰 것" (this, that, something to eat, a big one).
"것" also means "thing, one": "이것, 그것, 먹을 것, 큰 것" (this, that, something to eat, a big one).
dl: 샘 씨는 쉬는 날에 뭐 하는 걸 좋아해요?
Sam, what do you like to do on your days off?
saem ssineun swineun nare mwo haneun geol joahaeyo?
저는 축구하는 걸 좋아해요. 민하 씨는요?
I like playing soccer. What about you, Minha?
jeoneun chukkuhaneun geol joahaeyo minha ssineunyo?
저는 집에서 영화 보는 걸 좋아해요.
I like watching movies at home.
jeoneun jibeseo yeonghwa boneun geol joahaeyo
sm: "Verb + -는 것" means "verb + -ing".
"Verb + -는 것" means "verb + -ing".

i: "-기"도 동사를 명사처럼 만듭니다. "쉽다, 어렵다, 좋다, 편하다, 힘들다" 앞에서 "~하기에 어떠하다"는 뜻으로 씁니다.
"-기" also turns a verb into a noun. Before "쉽다, 어렵다, 좋다, 편하다, 힘들다" it means "easy/hard/good… to do".
m: 동사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-기"를 붙입니다. 받침과 관계없습니다.
Take "-다" off the verb and add "-기". It does not depend on 받침.
e: This laptop is easy to use.
This neighborhood is a good place to live.
It's hot today, so it's hard to study.
tp: The order is the opposite of English "hard to learn": add "-기" to the verb and put "어렵다, 쉽다" after it. "hard to learn" = "배우기 어려워요".
The order is the opposite of English "hard to learn": add "-기" to the verb and put "어렵다, 쉽다" after it. "hard to learn" = "배우기 어려워요".
목록, 제목, 메모에서는 "-기"로 끝냅니다. "말하기, 듣기, 읽기, 쓰기", "과제 내기", "손 씻기".
In lists, titles and notes, end with "-기": "말하기 (speaking), 듣기 (listening), 읽기 (reading), 쓰기 (writing)", "과제 내기" (hand in the assignment), "손 씻기" (wash hands).
dl: How is your Korean study going?

tp: To pass on "-아/어 주세요", use "-아/어 달라고 하다" (for the speaker) and "-아/어 주라고 하다" (for someone else): "도와 달라고 했어요" = He asked (me) to help him.
To pass on "-아/어 주세요", use "-아/어 달라고 하다" (for the speaker) and "-아/어 주라고 하다" (for someone else): "도와 달라고 했어요" = He asked (me) to help him.

No, he told me not to touch that one.

i: Used to pass on a suggestion. It is like "(He) suggested…, (He) said let's…" in English.

Take "-다" off the verb and add "-자고 해요/했어요". It does not depend on 받침. For "let's not", use "-지 말자고".

tp: "-(으)ㅂ시다, -아요/어요(같이), -(으)ㄹ까요?"를 전할 때 모두 "-자고 하다"가 됩니다.

a-isya ssi, gyosunimi oneul jeonyeogeul gachi meokjago hasyeosseoyo
학교 앞 삼겹살집에서 여섯 시에 만나자고 하셨어요.

i: Used to pass on someone else's question. It is like "(He) asked…" in English.

Take "-다" off and add "-냐고 하다/묻다/물어보다". For the past, use "-았/었냐고"; for nouns, use "(이)냐고".

tp: 네 가지 전하는 말을 함께 기억합니다. 말한 것 "-다고", 시킨 것 "-(으)라고", 같이 하자는 것 "-자고", 물은 것 "-냐고".
Remember the four reporting forms together: statements "-다고", orders "-(으)라고", suggestions "-자고", questions "-냐고".
못 알아들었을 때 "지금 뭐라고 하셨어요?"라고 다시 묻습니다.

I said I really want to take it.
sm: 물은 말은 "-냐고 물어봤어요"로 전합니다.
Pass on questions with "-냐고 물어봤어요".

i: 전하는 말을 줄인 모양입니다. 말할 때는 이 짧은 모양을 훨씬 많이 씁니다.

m: "-다고 해요 → -대요", "-(으)라고 해요 → -(으)래요", "-자고 해요 → -재요", "-냐고 해요 → -냬요", "(이)라고 해요 → (이)래요"입니다.
"-다고 해요 → -대요", "-(으)라고 해요 → -(으)래요", "-자고 해요 → -재요", "-냐고 해요 → -냬요", "(이)라고 해요 → (이)래요".
c: 오라고 해요 (He) tells you to come
휴일이라고 해요 (They) say it's a holiday

tp: It feels like English "I heard…, They say…", passing on what you heard.
It feels like English "I heard…, They say…", passing on what you heard.
"-(으)ㄹ래요" (your own wish) and "-(으)래요" (passing on an order) are different: "갈래요" (I'll go), "가래요" (He says to go).
"-(으)ㄹ래요" (your own wish) and "-(으)래요" (passing on an order) are different: "갈래요" (I'll go), "가래요" (He says to go).
지난 일은 "-았/었대요"입니다. "어제 조별 모임을 했대요."

dl: Yes, I heard there is. They say there's a make-up class.

sm: "-대요"는 "-다고 해요", "-(으)래요"는 "-(으)라고 해요"를 줄인 말입니다.
"-대요" is short for "-다고 해요", and "-(으)래요" is short for "-(으)라고 해요".
qz: "가래요"의 뜻은? I'll go / He says to go

i: Added to adjectives to show something gradually changes that way. It is like "get…, become…" (get colder) in English.

m: 형용사의 "-아요/어요" 모양에서 "요"를 떼고 "져요"를 붙입니다. 이미 바뀐 것은 "-아/어졌어요"입니다.
Take "요" off the adjective's "-아요/어요" form and add "져요". For something already changed, use "-아/어졌어요".

There have been more assignments lately.
I took medicine and got better.
to be fine, to be OK

형용사에만 붙습니다. 동사의 바뀜은 "-게 되다"입니다.
It is added only to adjectives. For change with verbs, use "-게 되다".
dl: Is your cold a bit better?
to be fine, to be OK

ne, geuraeseo gamgi geollin sarami manajeosseoyo
sm: "형용사 + -아/어지다"는 그렇게 바뀐다는 뜻입니다.
"Adjective + -아/어지다" means it changes to that.

i: Means things turned out that way, not by your own choice. It is like "came to…, ended up…, got to…" in English.
Means things turned out that way, not by your own choice. It is like "came to…, ended up…, got to…" in English.
m: 동사의 "-다"를 떼고 "-게 됐어요"를 붙입니다. 받침과 관계없습니다.
Take "-다" off the verb and add "-게 됐어요". It does not depend on 받침.
c: I came to know, I found out
I got to go, I ended up going
It turned out I can't go
e: I came to study in Korea.
I got to know Aisha at school.
처음에는 김치를 못 먹었는데 지금은 좋아하게 됐어요.
cheo-eumeneun gimchireul mot meogeonneunde jigeumeun joahage dwaesseoyo
At first I couldn't eat kimchi, but now I've come to like it.

tp: 정해진 일을 겸손하게 알릴 때 씁니다. "다음 달에 고향에 돌아가게 됐습니다." 인사말에 많습니다.
It is used to humbly announce something that has been decided: "다음 달에 고향에 돌아가게 됐습니다." (I will be going back home next month.) It is common in farewell speeches.
"형용사 + -아/어지다", "동사 + -게 되다"로 나누어 기억합니다.

dl: 샘 씨는 어떻게 한국에 오게 됐어요?
Sam, how did you come to Korea?
saem ssineun eotteoke han-guge oge dwaesseoyo?
I was accepted to Jeonju University, so I came.
How did you come to learn Korean?
I watched Korean dramas and came to like it.
sm: "동사 + -게 됐어요"는 일이 그렇게 되었다는 뜻입니다.
"Verb + -게 됐어요" means things came to be that way.

i: Means you do something and leave the result as it is. Used when preparing something in advance. It is like "leave it (open), do it in advance" in English.
Means you do something and leave the result as it is. Used when preparing something in advance. It is like "leave it (open), do it in advance" in English.
m: 동사의 "-아요/어요" 모양에서 "요"를 떼고 "놓다"를 붙입니다. "-아/어 두다"도 같은 뜻입니다.
Take "요" off the verb's "-아요/어요" form and add "놓다". "-아/어 두다" means the same.

tp: It is used much like English "leave… open, have… ready": "leave it open" = "열어 놓다".
It is used much like English "leave… open, have… ready": "leave it open" = "열어 놓다".
말할 때 "놓아"는 "놔"로 줄입니다. "열어 놔요", "해 놨어요".
In speech, "놓아" is shortened to "놔": "열어 놔요", "해 놨어요".
지시에서 자주 듣습니다. "미리 해 놓으세요", "여기에 놓아 두세요".

Sam, did you get the chairs ready for tomorrow morning?
saem ssi, nae-il achime sseul uijareul junbihae noasseoyo?
Yes, I stacked them in front of the lecture room.
잘했어요. 나갈 때 창문은 닫아 놓으세요.
Well done. When you leave, close the windows.
jalhaesseoyo nagal ttae changmuneun dada no-euseyo
sm: "Verb + -아/어 놓다" means "leave it…, do it in advance".
"Verb + -아/어 놓다" means "leave it…, do it in advance".

i: Means that after something is done, the state stays. It is like "is open, is sitting" in English.
Means that after something is done, the state stays. It is like "is open, is sitting" in English.

c: 켜지다 (a light) to be turned on
e: The professor is sitting over there.
tp: "-고 있다" is an action in progress; "-아/어 있다" is the state after it is done: "문을 열고 있어요" (I'm opening the door), "문이 열려 있어요" (The door is open).
"-고 있다" is an action in progress; "-아/어 있다" is the state after it is done: "문을 열고 있어요" (I'm opening the door), "문이 열려 있어요" (The door is open).
누가 해 놓은 것은 "-아/어 놓다"(사람이 주어), 그 결과는 "-아/어 있다"(물건이 주어)입니다. "문을 열어 놓았어요. 문이 열려 있어요."
What someone did and left is "-아/어 놓다" (a person is the subject); the result is "-아/어 있다" (a thing is the subject): "문을 열어 놓았어요. 문이 열려 있어요." (I left the door open. The door is open.)
dl: Sam, did you check before leaving?

sm: "-아/어 있다"는 일이 끝난 뒤의 상태가 이어짐을 나타냅니다.
"-아/어 있다" shows that the state after an action stays.

i: 어간이 "ㅡ"로 끝나는 낱말은 "-아/어"가 붙을 때 "ㅡ"가 떨어집니다.
When a word's stem ends in "ㅡ", the "ㅡ" drops when "-아/어" is added.
m: "ㅡ"를 떼고, 그 앞 글자의 모음이 ㅏ나 ㅗ이면 "-아요", 그 밖이거나 앞 글자가 없으면 "-어요"를 붙입니다. 바쁘다 → 바빠요, 예쁘다 → 예뻐요, 쓰다 → 써요.
Drop "ㅡ". If the vowel of the syllable before it is ㅏ or ㅗ, add "-아요"; otherwise, or if there is no syllable before it, add "-어요": 바쁘다 → 바빠요, 예쁘다 → 예뻐요, 쓰다 → 써요.
e: I had a headache, so I took medicine.
tp: "-아/어"로 시작하는 말끝에서만 바뀝니다. "-고, -지만, -습니다, -(으)면" 앞에서는 바뀌지 않습니다. 바쁘고, 바쁩니다, 바쁘면.
It changes only before endings that start with "-아/어". It does not change before "-고, -지만, -습니다, -(으)면": 바쁘고, 바쁩니다, 바쁘면.
지난 일도 같습니다. 바빴어요, 아팠어요, 썼어요, 컸어요.

규칙이 예외 없이 지켜지므로 불규칙이 아니라 "탈락"이라고 합니다.
This rule has no exceptions, so it is called "탈락" (dropping), not "irregular".
dl: Sam, are you busy these days?
네, 많이 바빠요. 어제는 허리도 아팠어요.
Yes, very busy. Yesterday my back hurt too.
ne, mani bappayo eojeneun heorido apasseoyo
sm: "ㅡ"로 끝나는 어간은 "-아/어" 앞에서 "ㅡ"가 떨어집니다.
A stem ending in "ㅡ" drops "ㅡ" before "-아/어".

i: 어간이 ㄹ 받침으로 끝나는 낱말은 ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ으로 시작하는 말끝 앞에서 ㄹ이 떨어집니다.
When a word's stem ends in a ㄹ 받침, the ㄹ drops before endings that start with ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ.
m: 살다 + -ㅂ니다 → 삽니다, 살다 + -세요 → 사세요, 살다 + -는 → 사는, 살다 + -니까 → 사니까. "-(으)" 계열 말끝에서는 "으"를 넣지 않습니다(살면, 살러, 살려고).
살다 + -ㅂ니다 → 삽니다, 살다 + -세요 → 사세요, 살다 + -는 → 사는, 살다 + -니까 → 사니까. With "-(으)" endings, do not add "으" (살면, 살러, 살려고).
e: I don't know a single person.
to not have, to not be there
If you open the door, it gets cold.
tp: "-아요/어요, -고, -지만" 앞에서는 떨어지지 않습니다. 살아요, 살고, 살지만.
It does not drop before "-아요/어요, -고, -지만": 살아요, 살고, 살지만.
"-(으)ㄹ" 계열에서는 ㄹ이 하나만 남습니다. 살 거예요, 만들 수 있어요, 알 때.
With "-(으)ㄹ" endings, only one ㄹ remains: 살 거예요, 만들 수 있어요, 알 때.
자주 쓰는 ㄹ 받침 낱말: 살다, 알다, 만들다, 열다, 팔다, 놀다, 울다, 들다, 걸다, 멀다, 길다, 힘들다.
Common words with a ㄹ 받침: 살다, 알다, 만들다, 열다, 팔다, 놀다, 울다, 들다, 걸다, 멀다, 길다, 힘들다.
dl: Do you know anyone in Korea?
Yes, my older cousin lives in Jeonju.
sm: ㄹ 받침은 ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ 앞에서 떨어집니다.
A ㄹ 받침 drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ.

i: 어간이 ㅂ 받침으로 끝나는 형용사 가운데 많은 낱말은 모음 앞에서 ㅂ이 "우"로 바뀝니다.
Many adjectives whose stem ends in a ㅂ 받침 change ㅂ to "우" before a vowel.
m: 덥다 + -어요 → 더워요, 덥다 + -(으)면 → 더우면, 덥다 + -(으)ㄴ → 더운, 덥다 + -(으)니까 → 더우니까. "돕다, 곱다"만 "도와요, 고와요"가 됩니다.
덥다 + -어요 → 더워요, 덥다 + -(으)면 → 더우면, 덥다 + -(으)ㄴ → 더운, 덥다 + -(으)니까 → 더우니까. Only "돕다, 곱다" become "도와요, 고와요".
e: This box is heavy, so let's lift it together.
tp: 자음으로 시작하는 말끝 앞에서는 바뀌지 않습니다. 덥고, 덥지만, 덥습니다.
It does not change before endings that start with a consonant: 덥고, 덥지만, 덥습니다.
규칙대로 쓰는 ㅂ 받침 낱말도 있습니다. 입다 → 입어요, 잡다 → 잡아요, 좁다 → 좁아요, 씹다 → 씹어요.
Some words with a ㅂ 받침 follow the regular rule: 입다 → 입어요, 잡다 → 잡아요, 좁다 → 좁아요, 씹다 → 씹어요.
dl: 파키스탄 음식이 더 매워요. 그런데 한국 겨울은 너무 추워요.
Pakistani food is spicier. But the Korean winter is too cold.
pakiseutan eumsigi deo maewoyo geureonde han-guk gyeo-ureun neomu chuwoyo
sm: ㅂ 불규칙은 모음 앞에서 ㅂ이 "우"로 바뀝니다.
In ㅂ irregular words, ㅂ changes to "우" before a vowel.

i: 어간이 ㄷ 받침으로 끝나는 몇몇 동사는 모음 앞에서 ㄷ이 ㄹ로 바뀝니다.
Some verbs whose stem ends in a ㄷ 받침 change ㄷ to ㄹ before a vowel.
m: 듣다 + -어요 → 들어요, 듣다 + -(으)면 → 들으면, 듣다 + -(으)세요 → 들으세요, 듣다 + -었어요 → 들었어요.
듣다 + -어요 → 들어요, 듣다 + -(으)면 → 들으면, 듣다 + -(으)세요 → 들으세요, 듣다 + -었어요 → 들었어요.

ㄷ 받침 verbs that follow the regular rule: 닫다 → 닫아요, 받다 → 받아요, 믿다 → 믿어요, 얻다 → 얻어요.

죄송합니다. 잘 못 들었습니다. 다시 말씀해 주세요.
I'm sorry. I didn't hear it well. Please say it again.
joesonghamnida jal mot deureotseumnida dasi malsseumhae juseyo

Load these boxes onto that truck. And ask if there's anything you don't know.
i sangjadeureul jeo teureoge sireuseyo moreuneun geon mureobogoyo
sm: ㄷ 불규칙은 모음 앞에서 ㄷ이 ㄹ로 바뀝니다.
In ㄷ irregular words, ㄷ changes to ㄹ before a vowel.

i: 어간이 "르"로 끝나는 낱말은 "-아/어" 앞에서 "ㅡ"가 떨어지고 ㄹ이 하나 더 생깁니다.
For words whose stem ends in "르", before "-아/어" the "ㅡ" drops and one more ㄹ is added.
m: "르" 앞 글자의 모음이 ㅏ나 ㅗ이면 "-ㄹ라요", 그 밖이면 "-ㄹ러요"가 됩니다. 모르다 → 몰라요, 빠르다 → 빨라요, 부르다 → 불러요.
If the vowel before "르" is ㅏ or ㅗ, it becomes "-ㄹ라요"; otherwise "-ㄹ러요": 모르다 → 몰라요, 빠르다 → 빨라요, 부르다 → 불러요.
e: The subway is faster than the bus.
Korea and Greece have different cultures.
tp: "-아/어" 앞에서만 바뀝니다. 모르고, 모르면, 모릅니다, 모르는.
It changes only before "-아/어": 모르고, 모르면, 모릅니다, 모르는.
지난 일: 몰랐어요, 빨랐어요, 불렀어요, 잘랐어요, 눌렀어요.
Past: 몰랐어요, 빨랐어요, 불렀어요, 잘랐어요, 눌렀어요.
"배가 불러요"는 "I'm full", "노래를 불러요"는 "I sing a song", "이름을 불러요"는 "I call a name"입니다.
"배가 불러요" means "I'm full", "노래를 불러요" means "I sing a song", and "이름을 불러요" means "I call (someone's) name".
dl: 샘 씨, 이 키오스크 쓸 줄 알아요?
Sam, do you know how to use this kiosk?
(-ㄹ 줄 알다 = to know how to)
saem ssi, i kioseukeu sseul jul arayo?
아니요, 잘 몰라요. 전에 쓰던 것하고 달라요.
No, I don't really know. It's different from the one I used before.
aniyo, jal mollayo jeone sseudeon geotago dallayo
먼저 이 빨간 버튼을 눌러요. 모르는 게 있으면 저를 불러요.
First press this red button. If there is anything you don't know, call me.
meonjeo i ppalgan beoteuneul nulleoyo moreuneun ge isseumyeon jeoreul bulleoyo
sm: "르" 낱말은 "-아/어" 앞에서 "ㄹ라/ㄹ러"가 됩니다.
"르" words become "ㄹ라/ㄹ러" before "-아/어".

i: 어간이 ㅅ 받침으로 끝나는 몇몇 낱말은 모음 앞에서 ㅅ이 떨어집니다.
Some words whose stem ends in a ㅅ 받침 drop the ㅅ before a vowel.
m: 낫다 + -아요 → 나아요, 낫다 + -(으)면 → 나으면, 낫다 + -았어요 → 나았어요. ㅅ이 떨어져도 모음을 줄이지 않습니다("나요"가 아니라 "나아요").
낫다 + -아요 → 나아요, 낫다 + -(으)면 → 나으면, 낫다 + -았어요 → 나았어요. Even when ㅅ drops, the vowels are not shortened ("나아요", not "나요").
c: to happen, to occur (고장 나다 = to break down)
e: I plan to build a house in my hometown.
Pour in water and stir well.
tp: 자음 앞에서는 바뀌지 않습니다. 낫고, 낫지만, 낫습니다.
It does not change before a consonant: 낫고, 낫지만, 낫습니다.
규칙대로 쓰는 ㅅ 받침 낱말: 씻다 → 씻어요, 벗다 → 벗어요, 웃다 → 웃어요.
ㅅ 받침 words that follow the regular rule: 씻다 → 씻어요, 벗다 → 벗어요, 웃다 → 웃어요.
병원에서 자주 씁니다. "언제 나아요?"(When will it get better?), "빨리 나으세요"(Get well soon), "부었어요"(It's swollen).
Often used at the hospital: "언제 나아요?" (When will it get better?), "빨리 나으세요" (Get well soon), "부었어요" (It's swollen).
dl: What's bothering you? (Where does it hurt?)

뼈는 괜찮습니다. 일주일쯤 쉬면 나을 거예요.

to be fine, to be OK
ppyeoneun gwaenchansseumnida ilju-iljjeum swimyeon na-eul kkeoyeyo
sm: ㅅ 불규칙은 모음 앞에서 ㅅ이 떨어집니다.
In ㅅ irregular words, ㅅ drops before a vowel.

i: 색깔을 나타내는 말과 "이렇다, 그렇다, 저렇다, 어떻다"는 모음 앞에서 ㅎ이 떨어지고 모양이 바뀝니다.
Color words and "이렇다, 그렇다, 저렇다, 어떻다" drop ㅎ and change form before a vowel.
m: "-아/어" 앞에서는 ㅎ이 떨어지고 "ㅐ"가 됩니다(빨갛다 → 빨개요, 어떻다 → 어때요). 하얗다만 "ㅒ"가 됩니다(하얘요). "-(으)" 앞에서는 ㅎ만 떨어집니다(빨갛다 → 빨간, 그렇다 → 그러면).
Before "-아/어", ㅎ drops and the vowel becomes "ㅐ" (빨갛다 → 빨개요, 어떻다 → 어때요). Only 하얗다 becomes "ㅒ" (하얘요). Before "-(으)", only ㅎ drops (빨갛다 → 빨간, 그렇다 → 그러면).
c: to be so, be like that
tp: 자음 앞에서는 바뀌지 않습니다. 빨갛고, 그렇지만, 어떻게 [어떠케].
It does not change before a consonant: 빨갛고, 그렇지만, 어떻게 [어떠케].
"좋다, 놓다, 넣다, 많다"는 규칙대로 씁니다. 좋아요, 놓아요, 넣어요.
"좋다, 놓다, 넣다, 많다" follow the regular rule: 좋아요, 놓아요, 넣어요.
"그래요, 그러면, 그런데, 그래서, 그러니까"는 모두 "그렇다"에서 나온 말입니다.
"그래요, 그러면, 그런데, 그래서, 그러니까" all come from "그렇다".
dl: 이 세탁기는 빨간 불이 켜지면 문을 열면 안 돼요.
On this washing machine, when the red light comes on, you must not open the door.
i setakkineun ppalgan buri kyeojimyeon muneul yeolmyeon an dwaeyo
The yellow light means it will finish soon.
to know (알겠습니다 = I understand, got it)
sm: ㅎ 불규칙은 모음 앞에서 ㅎ이 떨어집니다. 빨갛다 → 빨개요, 빨간.
In ㅎ irregular words, ㅎ drops before a vowel: 빨갛다 → 빨개요, 빨간.

i: 같은 뜻을 여러 문형으로 말할 수 있습니다. 누구에게, 어디에서 말하는지에 따라 알맞은 것을 고릅니다.
The same meaning can be said with several patterns. Choose the right one for who you are talking to and where.
m: 문형은 뜻으로 묶어서 기억합니다. 시킴, 금지, 허락, 해야 함, 까닭, 조건, 바람, 미루어 생각함. 아래 표에서 한 줄은 뜻이 같거나 가까운 문형입니다.

Remember the patterns in groups by meaning: orders, prohibition, permission, obligation, reason, condition, wishes, guessing. In the table below, each row has patterns with the same or similar meaning.
e: Don't touch it. You must not touch it.
I couldn't go because I was sick.
It's dangerous, so please be careful.
tp: 학교에서 가장 안전한 말투는 교수님께 "-습니다/-습니까", 친구에게 "-아요/어요"입니다. 반말은 상대가 먼저 권할 때만 씁니다.
At school, the safest speech style is "-습니다/-습니까" with professors and "-아요/어요" with friends. Use casual speech (반말) only when the other person suggests it first.
한국어와 영어의 가장 큰 차이 세 가지: ① 동사가 끝에 온다 ② 조사가 명사 뒤에 붙는다(영어의 전치사는 명사 앞에 온다) ③ "will, want to, must, don't, if"에 해당하는 말이 모두 동사 뒤에 붙는다.

The three biggest differences between Korean and English: ① The verb comes at the end. ② Particles come after nouns (English prepositions come before nouns). ③ The words for "will, want to, must, don't, if" all come after the verb.
dl: 샘 씨, 내일 일찍 올 수 있어요?
Sam, can you come early tomorrow?
saem ssi, nae-il iljjik ol su isseoyo?
네, 올 수 있습니다. 몇 시까지 오면 됩니까?
Yes, I can come. By what time should I come?
ne, ol su itseumnida myeot sikkaji omyeon doemnikka?
일곱 시까지 와야 해요. 늦으면 안 돼요.
You have to come by seven. You must not be late.
ilgop sikkaji waya haeyo neujeumyeon an dwaeyo
I understand. I will make sure not to be late.
to know (알겠습니다 = I understand, got it)
sm: 뜻이 같은 문형을 묶어서 기억하고, 듣는 사람에 맞는 말투를 고릅니다.
Remember patterns with the same meaning as a group, and choose the speech style that fits the listener.
